newsitem.title: USA: Dell sees 20 pct PC industry growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Dell sees 20 pct PC industry growth in '97.

text.p: Dell Computer Corp Chairman and Chief Executive Michael Dell said Thursday he expects the worldwide personal computer industry to grow about 20 percent this year, and his own company to grow even more.
His industry growth prediction is slightly above most forecasts. International Data Corp, for example, looks for growth of 17 percent in 1997.
Dell said he expects his company, which is the leading direct supplier of PCs, to continue to surpass industry growth rates this year.
Dell said 1997 PC industry growth would be fueled by new chip technologies such as Intel Corp's multimedia processor and the new Pentium II chip.
"This year we expect close to 20 percent growth because of the Pentium II and MMX," Dell said, after addressing an analyst meeting here.
Dell said that for the rest of the decade, he expects the PC industry to grow in a range of 15 to 20 percent.
He added that Dell Computer will continue to outpace industry growth rates, but he declined to be more specific.
Dell Chief Financial Officer Tom Meredith also declined to comment on the company's financials at the analyst meeting.
"We are pleased with our position in the marketplace and we look forward to a very strong year," Meredith told Reuters.
In his presentation to the analysts, Meredith highlighted Dell's fiscal 1997 achievements, such as its revenue growth of 47 percent and a 91 percent jump in net income.
"It was a tremendous year," he said.
He said Dell's stock had risen 246 percent in the past year, versus Intel's rise of 112 percent and Microsoft Corp's 87 percent.
He declined to comment on the current quarter. According to First Call, the Wall Street consensus estimate for Dell's first fiscal quarter, ending in April, is $0.92 a share, versus $0.42 a year ago.
